title: two pre-commit guards take their population from the worktree or ambient index, so any node's uncommitted work blocks every other node
body:
**TWO PRE-COMMIT GUARDS TAKE THEIR POPULATION FROM THE WORKTREE OR THE AMBIENT INDEX RATHER THAN FROM THE COMMIT BEING MADE, SO ANY NODE'S UNCOMMITTED WORK BLOCKS EVERY OTHER NODE'S COMMITS.**

Both measured 2026-08-30 in the shared checkout, both while the guard was CORRECT about its own subject.

**INSTANCE 1 -- `runner_roster_check.sh` reads the AMBIENT INDEX.** dc staged a new `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/absent_at_check.sh` while its roster row was still uncommitted. Every node's commit reddened -- ic's carrying only TUI files, cc's carrying `backup.enabled`, vc's carrying a board. **Run standalone the same tool PASSES**: `roster: 68 parity file(s) in this commit, all rostered ... every disposition matches the runner`. `git commit --only <one path>` builds HEAD-plus-that-path and cannot contain dc's file, and the guard reds anyway.

**INSTANCE 2 -- `view_skew_check.sh` reads the WORKTREE.** ic created an UNTRACKED `intent/st/ST0056/parity/ac-09_6-mcp-facade-read.md`. Nobody staged it, nobody was committing it, and it blocks every commit in the tree:

    skew: apparatus view(s) with no registered generator -- classify them or state why they stand alone:
      intent/st/ST0056/parity/ac-09_6-mcp-facade-read.md

**`git commit --only` CANNOT REACH EITHER, AND NOT FOR THE REASON THE SHARED-INDEX CLASS NAMES.** The canon-extract hazard is *foreign bytes inside a file that is legitimately mine to commit*, and path-scoping fails there because the bytes are not a separate path. **These two are simpler and worse: the file is not in the commit at all.** Path-scoping is irrelevant when the guard never looked at the commit.

**BLAST RADIUS IS WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE REST OF THE CLASS.** Index contention involves two nodes and fails loudly on `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`. Coherence -- a half-landed pair -- is a genuine property of the tree and arguably SHOULD block. **This blocks every node from work that was never offered for review**, including a file its author may be about to delete.

**BOTH GUARDS ARE ASKING A WELL-FORMED QUESTION ABOUT THE WRONG TREE.** The fix is a population, not a predicate: examine the paths in the commit being made, the way `canon_commit_check.sh` already does -- it narrows explicitly to *the attachment path(s) whose bytes or whose thread's canon THIS COMMIT changed* and says so in its output. **The pattern is already in the estate; two guards do not follow it.**

**NOT A TAG-WINDOW FIX.** Changing what a gate examines is exactly the change that arrives with no room for its own second fix, and the workaround -- wait for the peer to land, which is correct behaviour anyway -- costs minutes rather than correctness. Filed so the cost is recorded rather than re-diagnosed by whoever hits it next; three of four nodes hit one of these today and each diagnosed it independently.
